reviews.comment: Very easy class. 2 assignments and one group project at the end (can all be completed within an hour) which are all graded nicely. Lectures consist mostly of participation activities. Class is generally boring but not dry.

The prompt asks to list the professor's abilities. I think it would be more worthwhile to list her inabilities. BE READY TO BE CONFUSED ALL THE TIME. For someone who worked at NASA, she sure doesn't know a lot about anything...

Dr. Shryock is a great lecturer that knows the content and answers questions well. However, there is so much busy work such as projects, news, experiential, etc that doesn't help with understanding the content. She also doesn't make it clear what to expect on quizzes/exams. Despite this, if you do the work and go to office hours an A is manageable.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favourite TAMU professor. Made the class very interesting, and barely had to study outside of class because of how easy it was to learn and retain the knowledge taught in class.

ENGR181 is a great introduction to the Engineering Honors Program and Dr Shryock did a great job of outlining expectations for being in the program. As a pass/fail course I was not expecting it to be so engaging and useful but it definitely was. Dr Shryock gave us lots of great resources to use to succeed as EH students
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's the GOAT, gives great engaging lectures, explains concepts in simple easy to easy-to-understand ways, and cares about her students.  The only drawback I have is with the course itself specifically the exams and quizzes being online, but in the classroom leaving you with little room on the desk and you have to show work by typing into the box.
Class was easy, light homework (just one paper and some other small assignments), and prof doesn't really care what you do in class

If you choose to pay attention, the class is interesting. Because the course is basically an intro to engineering honors, most in my section zoned out and ended up wasting two hours every week because of it. The work is very minimal with the exception of a miniature literature review at the end. Shryock is an engaging and passionate teacher.

Shryock is an overall great professor. She's passionate about what she teaches and is great at engaging with the class. The only critique I have is the exam and quiz content. On one quiz she had a trick question and on the final, a lot of the questions were from a movie we had to watch. A little frustrating, but overall a great professor.

Love Dr. Shyock. Very fun to have in class and the content is easy to understand. In class examples are what she pulls from for quizzes. She wants you to be able to digest the concepts and not be able to just plug and chug numbers but in a good way. Office hours are super helpful but you HAVE to read the book. Make sure to ask about research!

I have a problem with the way the class is setup, because it just skims through many concepts, so it feels like I was just memorizing concepts instead of fully understanding them; however, I think Dr. Shryock tries her best. In class you work through problems, but unfortunately I always never could finish them before we moved to the next one.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is super nice and gives entretaining lectures. 201 is designed to have lots of assignments no matter who you take, but it is definitely the most annoying part of the class because you have to dedicate a lot of time. However, the class definitely makes you want to stay in AERO. NO chances for extra credit. Only 2 exams

ENGR 181 during Spring Semester. The main TA leads the majority of the class. Prof Shryock speaks at the beginning of the class. She also provides input here and there. The assignments are easy completion grades. Attendance is mandatory. Don't miss class because you will need to make it up the following semester. No quick make-ups for attendance.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a very annoying, honors lecture-based class with odd requirements for assignments and participation. Very boring.

For a seminar class, I had a lot more fun in this one than in other classes. She is a very nice person and very clear about what she expects. The class is kind of helpful in teaching us some important things, and she did a good job of letting us participate without having to speak. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up you will be fine

Very disorganized class. Many assignments were left ungraded at the end of the semester so hard to know what actually counts. Rarely responds to emails and if she does the response can be arrogant or or plain rude. Worst of all, the final exam had little to do with anything we learned in class. Overall a huge disappointment given her high ratings.

Dr. Shryock made ENGR181 pretty interesting, and from what I've heard she did a much better job running it than other professors have in the past. I did find that enjoyment of the class will depend on the other students more than it will on the professor. When we're in person again, try to sit next to non-annoying people.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of quizzes, homework, assignments, etc. that make up more than half your grade and are a good chance to get a better grade in the class. The tests on the other hand are very hard and she doesn't post solutions and is very hard to contact outside of class. At the end of the semester there will be missing grades, even the final.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitely try to take Dr. Shryock for AERO 201. There are lots of small quizzes that can make up for the inevitable mistakes on exams. She is also very good about dropping low grades. Very kind professor and is willing to help you if you fall behind.
She's easily the best professor I've had so far. she makes lectures enjoyable and makes sure everyone understands the material before moving on.
She is easily one of the best AERO professors at A&M and is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. Do whatever you can to get into her class.

Dr. Shryock is the bomb diggidy, I love her. She's the reason I decided to major in Aerospace. This class, however, is deceptively difficult. Just cause she's laid back doesn't mean you can slack, if you put in the effort you'll get an A. Read all the chapters, study the modules for quizzes, and study both reading and quizzes for exams.

While the number of quizzes taken in the class is unbelievable, Dr. Shryock makes AERO 201 interesting and enjoyable. If you study what she tells you too, it's an easy A. Large portions of the class are also free 100's (homework, activities). Get ready to read the textbook (it is pretty interesting though so it's not too bad).
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Shryock is always in a cheerful mode and is extremely passionate about the subject she teaches. She explains topics clearly and is willing to give extra credit to the class. Helped me to find a passion for airplanes, something that didn't interest me at all before this class
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Shryock has a very positive attitude and is really there to help you. She has a flipped classroom, so you have to read the book and learn the material outside of class, and then you are quizzed on the modules first thing in class, and she will do examples after. Her exams can be kind of tricky if you don't know what to study.
Kristi SHryock will probably be your best teacher sophomore year of AERO. She's really nice and helpful.
